(Olivier Acuna/CoinDesk)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Fb18ee53b50842f9ee6f7eb1059651463c7e51c9a-765x430.jpg%3Frect%3D1%2C0%2C764%2C430%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) Summary * JPMorgan and Citi process trillions of dollars through blockchain systems, but their tokenized payment services remain largely limited to institutional customers and permissioned networks. * Monument Bank plans to tokenize up to 250 million pounds of interest-bearing retail deposits on Midnight, using zero-knowledge proofs to protect customer data while meeting regulatory requirements. * The project aims to give consumers access to tokenized investments and lending through a conventional banking app without requiring them to understand or directly use cryptocurrency. JPMorgan moves more than $3 trillion through its [Kinexys blockchain platform](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/06/29/j-p-morgan-broadens-blockchain-settlement-network-as-banks-modernize-cross-border-payments), and Citi Token Services processes billions in cross-border payments daily. Both are great examples of Wall Street giants modernizing their legacy systems and adopting blockchain for cross-border payments; however, neither of them is for the regular person with a savings account. That gap is not an accident. summary: Title: Zcash targets November upgrade to make private payments up to three times faster URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/09/18/zcash-targets-november-upgrade-to-make-private-payments-up-to-three-times-faster Published Time: 2026-09-18T12:50:01.701Z Markdown Content: 2 days ago 2 min read ![Image 1: Computer, network upgrade (JESHOOTS-com/Pixabay)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F837700a2c31b20bd836c2e16853b6d25f4e30f7f-5400x3600.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C281%2C5400%2C3038%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) (JESHOOTS-com/Pixabay) Summary * Zcash developers are targeting Nov. 5 for the NU7 upgrade, which would cut block times to 25 seconds from 75 seconds and make private payments faster. * NU7 would temporarily remove about 60% of transaction fees from circulation, with the funds scheduled to return as mining rewards beginning in February 2031. * The upgrade preserves Zcash’s issuance and halving schedule by reducing rewards per block and tripling the halving interval, while its final activation decision is due Oct. 20. Zcash developers are [targeting Nov. 5 an upgrade](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655) that would cut the time between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 to go live. The NU7 upgrade would also begin setting aside part of the network’s transaction fees for future mining rewards. The timetable follows talks among the core builder teams Zcash Foundation, Project Tachyon, Valar, ZODL and Shielded Labs. The groups and engineering teams reached unanimous agreement on the upgrade’s contents after a series of community and coinholder polls. About 2.4 million ZEC participated in the vote, equal to 66% of the eligible pool. Some 98.9% backed keeping Zcash’s existing halving schedule, while 96.6% chose February 2031 as the starting point for returning collected fees to miners.
